luna: The section’s image depends on ground that gives growth. This ayah adds enclosed gardens to the sequence of what the earth brings forth, extending the scene from staple crop to cultivated abundance. | terra: Dense gardens show the completed growth of the sequence.

luna: The section asks what a field’s care can yield. This ayah names fruit and pasture, completing a list of nourishment provided for people and animals. | terra: Fruit and pasture name further forms of what the tended earth gives.

luna: The section says land’s growth is a gift that can be received and forgotten. This ayah concludes that food and enjoyment are for people and their livestock, naming the recipients of the provision. | terra: The whole rain-and-field sequence is declared provision for people and their cattle.
luna: The section says the buried will be raised and what is concealed will be exposed. This ayah says the records will be spread open, a direct judgment-day disclosure.
luna: The section says the Rabb is fully informed and the contents of chests will be exposed. This ayah says every soul will know what it has brought forward, connecting disclosure to personal deeds.

luna: The section asks what it means to be ungrateful to one’s Rabb after receiving care and gifts. This direct address asks what deludes the human against the generous Lord, joining the same human, Rabb, and forgotten generosity. | terra: The human is asked what deceived him concerning his generous Lord, bringing the section's human, giving generosity, and forgotten Rabb into one address.
terra: The generous Lord of 82:6 created, proportioned, and balanced the human, spelling out the care to which the human is ungrateful.
terra: God assembles the human in whatever form He wills, continuing the proportioning and balancing care of 82:7.
terra: After the generous Lord's formation, people nevertheless deny judgment, showing care answered by denial.

luna: The section says the Rabb is fully informed of people’s deeds. This ayah says guardians are appointed over them, giving a concrete form to the witnessed record. | terra: Guardians are appointed over people, introducing the record of conduct that follows denial of judgment.

luna: The section develops a witness grounded in knowledge. This ayah calls the recorders noble writers, identifying who preserves what is done. | terra: The guardians are noble writers, giving durable form to the testimony over conduct.

luna: The section says those who cut the bond remain within the Rabb’s knowledge. This ayah says the recorders know what people do, a specific witness to their conduct. | terra: The recorders know what people do, adding informed testimony to the generous Lord's prior care.
luna: The section says the human will be raised and brought to account. This ayah describes the person who receives his record in his right hand, a specific form of that accounting.

luna: The section’s final ayah places the Rabb’s knowledge on the day of reckoning. This ayah promises an easy account; 84:9 supplies the return to family, while this row contributes the ease of the reckoning.
luna: The section asks whether the human knows that he will be raised and exposed. This ayah describes the record-holder returning joyful to his family, a concrete result of the reckoning.

luna: The section says the human’s inward contents will be disclosed and the Rabb knows all. This ayah describes a person receiving his record behind his back, the contrary outcome to the right-hand record in 84:7.
luna: The section says the human will face the result of what he concealed and did. This ayah gives the record-holder’s response of calling for destruction, a particular reaction to disclosure.
luna: The section’s image ends with the Rabb fully informed on that day. This ayah names the record-holder’s destination in the blazing fire, a specific consequence of the account.

luna: The section describes human attachment to worldly good and later exposure. This ayah says the person had been joyful among his family, contrasting ease before death with the judgment that follows.
luna: The section asks whether a person knows he will be raised. This ayah says the person thought he would never return to God, naming the ignorance that the section challenges.

luna: The section says the Rabb is fully informed about people on that day. This ayah says the Lord was ever seeing him, directly grounding the reckoning in divine awareness. | terra: A person who thought he would never return is corrected because his Lord was always seeing him, another form of inescapable lordly knowledge.
luna: The section brings what is inside the chest to account in 100:10. This ayah names the day when hidden things are tested and exposed, a direct parallel to disclosed inward contents.
terra: The command to glorify the name of one's Lord gives the fitting response to the creating, measuring, guiding, and pasture-producing care of 87:2-4.

luna: The section defines Rabb’s nurturing as creating successively and bringing toward completion. This ayah says God created and proportioned, naming formation as an ordered act of care. | terra: The Lord creates and proportionally fashions, one concise description of care moving a thing toward completion.

luna: The section describes nurturing as measured development toward an end. This ayah says God decreed and guided, adding direction to the process of formation. | terra: He measures and guides, adding fitness and direction to the staged formation of 87:2.
terra: He brings forth pasture, applying the creating and guiding Lord's care directly to plant growth.
terra: The pasture brought forth in 87:4 is made dark stubble, marking the limit and passing end of growth rather than kenud soil's refusal to grow at all.
terra: The Lord is declared ever watchful immediately before the human's mistaken readings of expanded and restricted provision in 89:15-16.

luna: The section describes a person measuring what he receives while forgetting the giver. This ayah says the person reads abundant provision as proof that his Lord honored him; it exposes one way gifts can be misread. | terra: When his Lord tests him by honoring and favoring him, the human says “my Lord has honored me,” reading lordship only through abundance.

luna: The section connects kenūd with counting hardship instead of remembering care. This ayah says a person reads restricted provision as proof that his Lord humiliated him, completing the mistaken measure begun in 89:15. | terra: When his Lord measures provision, the human says “my Lord has humiliated me,” counting restriction while failing to understand the test paired with 89:15.

luna: The section’s ingrate receives care but does not return it. This ayah rejects the claim that provision alone signals honor and names failure to honor the orphan, bringing the question of response into social action. | terra: The rebuke after the two provision-tests says people do not honor the orphan, showing failed gratitude in treatment of another dependent.

luna: The section’s kenūd figure breaks reciprocity after receiving gifts. This ayah says people do not urge one another to feed the poor, naming a withheld form of generosity. | terra: They do not urge one another to feed the poor, so received provision does not continue outward.
terra: They consume inheritance voraciously, preparing the charge of immense love of wealth in 89:20.

luna: The section’s word حبّ is paired with خير and its dictionary gloss includes gift or wealth. This ayah says people love wealth intensely (حبّ المال), giving a concrete instance of attachment to material good. | terra: The charge that people love wealth with immense حُبًّا closely restates severe love of al-khayr and explains why gift eclipses giver.
terra: The one who gives and is mindful embodies the continuing, generous response opposite the withholding kenud.
terra: Affirming the finest promise distinguishes the giver in 92:5 from the denier paired with withholding in 92:9.
terra: The giver is eased toward ease, the resulting path of the generous response in 92:5.
terra: The one who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient combines the two central failures of the section: stopping the gift's flow and forgetting dependence.
terra: The self-sufficient withholder denies the finest promise, adding denial to the stopped flow of 92:8.
terra: He is eased toward hardship, the consequence paired against the giver's ease in 92:7.
terra: The Lord promises to give until the recipient is satisfied, setting divine generosity before the remembered gifts later in the surah.
terra: The Lord's shelter of the orphan is a concrete stage of the nurturing history that grounds the duties in 93:9-11.
terra: Divine guidance supplies another stage of care remembered before the command to recount favor.

luna: The section’s Rab gloss includes sustaining and completing gifts. This ayah recalls that God found the Prophet in need and made him self-sufficient, a concrete instance of care provided rather than self-made. | terra: The Lord finds the addressee in need and enriches him, a concise instance of nurturing care and completed bounty.
terra: The former orphan who was sheltered must not oppress an orphan, so received care is required to continue toward another.
terra: The former needy recipient must not repel the one who asks, preserving rather than cutting the line of provision.

luna: The section asks what response a recipient owes the Rabb. This ayah commands the Prophet to speak of his Lord’s favor, a direct example of acknowledging the giver. | terra: The favor of one's Lord must be recounted, the direct opposite of forgetting blessings while remembering hardships.
terra: The first command is to read in the name of the Lord who created, identifying Rabb before the human's self-sufficient transgression in 96:6-7.
terra: The Lord creates the human from a clinging substance, specifying the humble beginning within 96:1's lordly creation.
terra: The command to read is repeated while the Lord is called the most generous, making 96:6-7 a rejection of acknowledged generosity.
terra: God teaches by the pen, one concrete means of the instruction completed in 96:5.
terra: God teaches the human what he did not know, completing the formative care that precedes the same human's transgression in 96:6.

luna: The section asks why a person is kenūd to his Rabb despite ongoing nurture. This ayah says the human transgresses, naming the response that follows. | terra: The same formula إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَانَ introduces the human's transgression, whose cause 96:7 identifies as imagined independence from care.

luna: The section’s claim of ingratitude is explained here: the human transgresses when he sees himself as self-sufficient (استغنى). It names the illusion that cuts the felt relation to the Rabb. | terra: The human transgresses because he sees himself as self-sufficient, naming the illusion by which a recipient forgets the nurturing Lord of 96:6.

luna: The section says the Rabb remains fully informed of those who cut the bond. This ayah says the earth will report its news on that day, adding the ground itself as a witness in the reckoning. | terra: Earth reports its news, turning the ground itself into a witness when hidden deeds are exposed.

luna: The section says the Rabb is fully informed on the day and allows the earth to serve as a witness. This ayah says the earth’s report comes by its Lord’s inspiration; 99:4 supplies the report itself, while this row explains its source. | terra: Earth reports because its Lord inspired it, joining Rabb to the ground's testimony.

luna: The section says the contents of the graves and chests will be brought out. This ayah says people will emerge in separate groups to be shown their deeds, completing the disclosure scene. | terra: People emerge separately to be shown their deeds, specifying what the earth's report leads to.

luna: The section moves from a human witness to the Rabb’s knowledge on the final day. This ayah says whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, making hidden conduct visible. | terra: Even an atom's weight of good is seen, so no return along the gift relation escapes disclosure.

luna: The section says the Rabb is fully informed of people on that day. This ayah says whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it, completing the exposure of what had seemed uncounted. | terra: Even an atom's weight of evil is seen, completing the exhaustive boundary of that disclosure.

luna: The section pairs intense love of خير with the opening of graves. This ayah says rivalry in accumulating more distracts people, connecting the section’s attachment to wealth with its warning about what lies beyond the grave.

luna: The section’s 100:8-9 moves from love of good to the graves being opened. This ayah says rivalry lasts until people visit the graves, supplying a close parallel between wealth-seeking and delayed awareness.

luna: The section says the Rabb will be fully informed about people on that day. This ayah says people will be questioned about نعيم, directly connecting received favor to the reckoning. | terra: People will be questioned that day about enjoyed bounty, joining the loved gift to the knowing accountability it cannot escape.

luna: The section says the human clings intensely to خير and forgets the giver. This ayah depicts a person gathering wealth and counting it, a specific, though indirect, picture of attachment that measures possession rather than relationship. | terra: The person who gathers and repeatedly counts wealth embodies love of the gift and a distorted practice of counting, though the section's kenud counts afflictions instead.
terra: He supposes his wealth makes him last forever, extending the self-sufficiency produced by counted possessions in 104:2.
terra: The recipients are told to worship the Lord of the House, directing response to the owner behind the provisions in 106:4.
terra: That Lord feeds against hunger and gives safety against fear, two concrete favors that explain the worship commanded in 106:3.
terra: God announces that He has given abundance, placing a great gift before the response commanded in 108:2.
terra: Prayer and sacrifice are directed to one's Lord because of the abundance in 108:1, an explicit gift-to-giver return.
